chapter: Follow-up questions, Bird and the Ellington sidemen
title: Timme Rosencrantz, Inez Cavanaugh and never getting a bad review
summary: Jones recalls Danish baron Timme Rosencrantz and his companion Inez Cavanaugh, who was down and out in 1973, and says he has never had a bad review.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Around there. I had those things, and I got them when I first got to New York. Timmy Rosencrantz had them and they were black market.
Uh-huh.
And I was able to talk Timmy and Inez Cavanaugh, and talk them out of them so I could put it on tape, you know.
Tell me about Timmy.
Well, let's see, he just promoted jazz over there in Denmark while he was alive, you know.
Uh-huh.
And he would go back and forth, you know, between Denmark and New York, and I think he was a Baron or something.
Yes.
He had a title.
Yeah, I've heard that.
But you wouldn't know it around the White Rose Bar, because he was just as drunk as we were, you
know? But he used to like to hang out with us, you know, and the last time I saw him was in Copenhagen, before -- you know, he wasn't well then. Then later on I found out about his passing, you know.
Inez was out here in '73.
Inez?
Yeah, she was very -- she wasn't well at all.
I thought she was gone.
Well, in '73 she was here because she called Duke when he was in the hospital here at -- was it St. Vincent's, when he had the pneumonia.
Yeah, when we were doing the show?

Yeah. And he asked me to go see her, go find her and bring her over to see him, and so I did. She was staying in a little five dollar a night place near the Hollywood Ranch Market, and so I picked her up and took her over to see him and he gave her some money. She was completely down and out and in fact desperate for some kind of work or something, and she wasn't well at all and so shortly after that, I brought her over here and fed her a couple of times, because she was just wiped out. And then Claire Gordon gave her a place to live for awhile, and then she moved on and I don't know what happened after that.
I thought she'd passed.
Well, the last time I heard from her was about '74, I guess.
The last time I saw her she was looking well, looked like she always did, back in New York, but it was in Italy, Milan, Italy, you know?
Uh-huh.
And I think she and Timmy had separated by that time and -- but she did her writing in the Metronome days and all those things, you know. With Barry Ulanov and all that gang of people.
Uh-huh.

Around that time, you know. And all those people have been very kind to me, on reviews and records. I can say this, as I've possibly said on one of the other tapes, had I thought about it I wouldn't have done it this way, but it's good that I didn't think about a goal.
Uh-huh.
I wasn't. I was just doing what I loved to do, and these people have never given me a bad review. Now, some of them have been better than others, but I've never had a bad review yet.
That's beautiful.
I'm getting scared of the first one.
(Laughter)
I'm overdue for one now.
